title: Replace wall-clock Future.delayed synchronization with deterministic waits in gamification staleness tests
why: 7 sites across 2 files (curriculum_breakdown_staleness_test.dart:66; points_providers_reactive_test.dart:61,68,100,111,154,164) synchronize on a Riverpod stream/FutureProvider re-emission by sleeping a fixed real-world duration instead of awaiting the actual event — the same feature area's achievements_overview_staleness_after_redemption_test.dart shows the deterministic alternative already in use (container.invalidate(...) + await container.read(provider.future)). A fixed delay is a flaky-under-CI-load bet: too short and a legitimately-fixed provider that happens to take longer intermittently fails the test; the tests exist specifically to pin reactive-update timing, so racing against the clock to verify timing is a contradiction in terms.
recommendation: Await the stream's next matching emission via a Completer or StreamQueue keyed on the expected value (or pumpEventQueue() for Drift's microtask-driven watch streams) instead of a fixed delay.
acceptance_criteria: Zero `Future<void>.delayed` calls remain in curriculum_breakdown_staleness_test.dart and points_providers_reactive_test.dart.
Both files pass 20 consecutive runs under --test-randomize-ordering-seed=random without flake.
